- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching.
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- humanizer: Remove signs of AI-generated writing from text. Use when editing or reviewing
text to make it sound more natural and human-written. Based on Wikipedia's
comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, negative
parallelisms, and excessive conjunctive phrases.
- openfort: Builds applications with Openfort using TypeScript SDK, Node, React Native, Unity. Use when working with Openfort embedded wallets, backend wallets and stablecoins.
- openfort: Builds applications with Openfort using TypeScript SDK (React, JS, Node). Use when working with Openfort embedded wallets, backend wallets and stablecoins.
- solidity-auditor: Security audit of Solidity code while you develop. Trigger on "audit", "check this contract", "review for security". Modes - default (full repo), DEEP (+ adversarial reasoning), or a specific filename.
- entry-point-analyzer:entry-points: Identifies state-changing entry points in smart contracts
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- ccc-skills:excalidraw: Generate architecture diagrams as .excalidraw files from codebase analysis. Use when the user asks to create architecture diagrams, system diagrams, visualize codebase structure, or generate excalidraw files.
- adversarial-spec:adversarial-spec: Iteratively refine a product spec by debating with multiple LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Grok, etc.) until all models agree. Use when user wants to write or refine a specification document using adversarial development.
- entry-point-analyzer:entry-point-analyzer: Analyzes smart contract codebases to identify state-changing entry points for security auditing. Detects externally callable functions that modify state, categorizes them by access level (public, admin, role-restricted, contract-only), and generates structured audit reports. Excludes view/pure/read-only functions. Use when auditing smart contracts (Solidity, Vyper, Solana/Rust, Move, TON, CosmWasm) or when asked to find entry points, audit flows, external functions, access control patterns, or privileged operations.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- statusline: Set up Claude Code's status line UI
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- insights: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions
- team-onboarding: Help teammates ramp on Claude Code with a guide from your usage

3	# v0.2.1 Openfort Implementation Part 2
4	
5	> Superseded by `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.2-openfort-implementation-with-onboarding.md`.  
6	> Use `v0.2.2` as the current source of truth for the Openfort rollout plan.
7	
8	**Date:** 2026-03-27
9	**Status:** Superseded
10	**Predecessor:** `docs-dev/audit-review/v0.2.0-openfort-integration-review-1.md`
11	
12	## Goal
13	
14	Finish the Openfort migration in `front-pro` as part of a coordinated frontend + backend move away from Particle.
15	
16	## Current State
17	
18	- Openfort provider wiring is active in the live app shell.
19	- `/login` uses `OpenfortButton`.
20	- Automatic Shield recovery endpoint is present.
21	- App-wide client auth/session bootstrapping and route guarding have been added.
22	- The header wallet entry point now uses Openfort-native UI instead of the legacy custom wallet modal flow.
23	- Legacy frontend auth proxy / localStorage / axios bearer-token utilities have been removed from the live path.
24	- `backpro` now exposes an Openfort-first auth contract:
25	  - `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
26	  - `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
27	  - `POST /v1/auth/logout`
28	  - `GET /v1/me`
29	  - `GET /v1/account/status`
30	  - `GET /v1/kyc/status`
31	- `backpro` now keys users by `openfort_user_id` and no longer keeps Particle in the active auth contract.
32	- The remaining blocker is environment setup: the required env vars / API keys are not configured yet, so real app testing cannot start until that is done.
33	
34	## Selected Direction
35	
36	- **Option B selected:** coordinated `front-pro` + `backpro` migration
37	- **Frontend branch of record:** `openfort`
38	- **Backend branch of record:** `openfort`
39	- **Frontend route policy:** all non-`/login` pages are treated as authenticated app pages
40	- **Wallet UX policy:** use Openfort stock UI/modal, remove custom wallet/login flow from the live path
41	- **External wallet policy:** keep WalletConnect / MetaMask support in the provider config; reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in a dedicated external-wallet phase
42	- **Greenfield policy:** there are no legacy users to migrate, so the Openfort branches may make contract/schema breaking changes instead of preserving the old Particle login shape
43	
44	## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context
45	
46	- This repo is the frontend half of the migration.
47	- The backend half lives in the sibling repo: `../backpro`
48	- Frontend task document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
49	- Backend companion document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
50	- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories, not from `develop`.
51	
52	## Branch Strategy
53	
54	### `front-pro`
55	
56	1. Preserve the current Openfort work on branch `openfort`
57	2. Recreate `develop` from commit `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`
58	3. Use `develop` as the Particle-era fallback line
59	4. Continue all Openfort migration work on `openfort`
60	
61	### `backpro`
62	
63	1. Create branch `openfort` from current `develop`
64	2. Leave `develop` unchanged
65	3. Continue all Openfort backend migration work on `openfort`
66	
67	## Current Frontend Surfaces Treated As Authenticated
68	
69	These routes currently exist in `src/app` and should be treated as app/private surfaces in this phase unless intentionally split later:
70	
71	- `/`
72	- `/home`
73	- `/explore-projects`
74	- `/create-project`
75	- `/tokenization`
76	- `/investment-portal`
77	- `/digital-assets`
78	- `/investor-management`
79	- `/investment-requests`
80	- `/asset-management`
81	- `/swap`
82	- `/kyc`
83	
84	Public/auth exception:
85	
86	- `/login`
87	
88	## Target Outcome
89	
90	1. Users authenticate through Openfort and remain authenticated across the app.
91	2. Protected app routes in `front-pro` respect auth state.
92	3. The header and wallet entry points use Openfort state/components instead of legacy mock flows.
93	4. Backend API access is aligned with an Openfort-compatible backend session model.
94	5. The app exposes a clear sign-in / sign-out / connected-wallet experience.
95	6. `backpro` preserves its JWT/refresh/session architecture while replacing Particle as the identity source.
96	
97	## Concrete Frontend ↔ Backend Contract For This Phase
98	
99	Use a dedicated backend session-exchange endpoint instead of reviving the old Particle login/register proxies:
100	
101	- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
102	  - frontend sends `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
103	  - token source is `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
104	  - request body is optional and should only carry app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
105	- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
106	  - uses the existing backend refresh-cookie flow
107	- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
108	  - revokes backend refresh session
109	- `GET /v1/me`
110	  - returns the backend user/profile/session view for the authenticated app shell
111	
112	Recommended frontend behavior:
113	
114	- after Openfort login succeeds, exchange the Openfort token for an InfraFund backend session
115	- keep the returned backend access token in memory, not `localStorage`
116	- call `backpro` directly from the browser with `credentials: 'include'`
117	- keep only the Openfort Shield recovery route in Next.js; do not keep the old auth proxy layer alive just to preserve Particle-era paths
118	
119	## Implementation Plan
120	
121	### Phase 1 — Repository preparation
122	
123	- Keep active work on `openfort` in both repositories
124	- Update this task document to reflect the approved coordinated plan
125	- Create a backend-specific task document under `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/`
126	
127	### Phase 2 — App-wide frontend auth integration
128	
129	- Use the `useUser()` hook from `@openfort/react` as the primary auth-state source
130	- Implement a **client-side layout guard** (not `middleware.ts`) since Openfort session state is SDK-based and not available server-side
131	- Redirect authenticated users away from `/login`
132	- Guard app routes so unauthenticated users are redirected to `/login`
133	- Add loading/fallback handling while Openfort resolves session state
134	- Treat the existing app-shell pages as private surfaces unless intentionally split into public pages later
135	- Remove `AuthProvider.WALLET` from the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` (will be reintroduced in the external wallet phase)
136	
137	### Phase 3 — Replace the live legacy wallet UX
138	
139	- Remove or retire `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx` from the header flow
140	- Replace the header wallet action with Openfort-native behavior:
141	  - `OpenfortButton`
142	  - Openfort stock modal/profile flow
143	- Ensure the live wallet entry point is consistent with the login experience
144	
145	### Phase 4 — User identity and sign-out
146	
147	- Replace hardcoded guest text in `src/components/header.tsx`
148	- Show user identity from Openfort state
149	- Confirm the stock Openfort account flow covers sign-out behavior cleanly
150	- Confirm the post-sign-out redirect and app state reset
151	
152	### Phase 5 — Frontend legacy auth cleanup ✓
153	
154	**Kept (Openfort-native):**
155	
156	- `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` — Shield recovery endpoint
157	
158	**Deleted (legacy Particle/BFF paths):**
159	
160	- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
161	- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
162	- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
163	- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
164	- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
165	- `src/app/api/deposit/route.ts`
166	- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
167	- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
168	- `src/utils/axios.utils.ts`
169	- `src/utils/server-axios.ts`
170	- `src/utils/get-server-url.ts`
171	- `src/services/api.service.ts`
172	
173	**Replaced by:**
174	
175	- `src/lib/backend-auth-client.ts` — fetch-based client for the new backend contract (`/auth/openfort/exchange`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`, `/me`)
176	
177	### Phase 6 — Backend auth migration dependency
178	
179	- `backpro` keeps its JWT/refresh/session architecture
180	- Replace Particle-specific auth inputs and validation
181	- Stop depending on `ParticleID` as the long-term auth identity key
182	- Replace it with a unique `openfort_user_id` key sourced from the validated Openfort session
183	- Validate the Openfort access token server-side against Openfort before issuing InfraFund JWTs
184	- Adopt the exchange endpoint described above as the single frontend → backend auth handshake
185	- Add first authenticated backend surfaces such as `/me` and account/KYC status
186	
187	### Phase 7 — External wallet support (WalletConnect / MetaMask)
188	
189	- Reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
190	- Verify WalletConnect project ID is configured and the connect flow works end-to-end
191	- Test MetaMask and other external wallet connections via `OpenfortWagmiBridge`

# v0.2.1 Openfort Implementation Part 2

> Superseded by `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.2-openfort-implementation-with-onboarding.md`.  
> Use `v0.2.2` as the current source of truth for the Openfort rollout plan.

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Status:** Superseded
**Predecessor:** `docs-dev/audit-review/v0.2.0-openfort-integration-review-1.md`

## Goal

Finish the Openfort migration in `front-pro` as part of a coordinated frontend + backend move away from Particle.

## Current State

- Openfort provider wiring is active in the live app shell.
- `/login` uses `OpenfortButton`.
- Automatic Shield recovery endpoint is present.
- App-wide client auth/session bootstrapping and route guarding have been added.
- The header wallet entry point now uses Openfort-native UI instead of the legacy custom wallet modal flow.
- Legacy frontend auth proxy / localStorage / axios bearer-token utilities have been removed from the live path.
- `backpro` now exposes an Openfort-first auth contract:
  - `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - `GET /v1/me`
  - `GET /v1/account/status`
  - `GET /v1/kyc/status`
- `backpro` now keys users by `openfort_user_id` and no longer keeps Particle in the active auth contract.
- The remaining blocker is environment setup: the required env vars / API keys are not configured yet, so real app testing cannot start until that is done.

## Selected Direction

- **Option B selected:** coordinated `front-pro` + `backpro` migration
- **Frontend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Backend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Frontend route policy:** all non-`/login` pages are treated as authenticated app pages
- **Wallet UX policy:** use Openfort stock UI/modal, remove custom wallet/login flow from the live path
- **External wallet policy:** keep WalletConnect / MetaMask support in the provider config; reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in a dedicated external-wallet phase
- **Greenfield policy:** there are no legacy users to migrate, so the Openfort branches may make contract/schema breaking changes instead of preserving the old Particle login shape

## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context

- This repo is the frontend half of the migration.
- The backend half lives in the sibling repo: `../backpro`
- Frontend task document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- Backend companion document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories, not from `develop`.

## Branch Strategy

### `front-pro`

1. Preserve the current Openfort work on branch `openfort`
2. Recreate `develop` from commit `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`
3. Use `develop` as the Particle-era fallback line
4. Continue all Openfort migration work on `openfort`

### `backpro`

1. Create branch `openfort` from current `develop`
2. Leave `develop` unchanged
3. Continue all Openfort backend migration work on `openfort`

## Current Frontend Surfaces Treated As Authenticated

These routes currently exist in `src/app` and should be treated as app/private surfaces in this phase unless intentionally split later:

- `/`
- `/home`
- `/explore-projects`
- `/create-project`
- `/tokenization`
- `/investment-portal`
- `/digital-assets`
- `/investor-management`
- `/investment-requests`
- `/asset-management`
- `/swap`
- `/kyc`

Public/auth exception:

- `/login`

## Target Outcome

1. Users authenticate through Openfort and remain authenticated across the app.
2. Protected app routes in `front-pro` respect auth state.
3. The header and wallet entry points use Openfort state/components instead of legacy mock flows.
4. Backend API access is aligned with an Openfort-compatible backend session model.
5. The app exposes a clear sign-in / sign-out / connected-wallet experience.
6. `backpro` preserves its JWT/refresh/session architecture while replacing Particle as the identity source.

## Concrete Frontend ↔ Backend Contract For This Phase

Use a dedicated backend session-exchange endpoint instead of reviving the old Particle login/register proxies:

- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - frontend sends `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
  - token source is `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
  - request body is optional and should only carry app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - uses the existing backend refresh-cookie flow
- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - revokes backend refresh session
- `GET /v1/me`
  - returns the backend user/profile/session view for the authenticated app shell

Recommended frontend behavior:

- after Openfort login succeeds, exchange the Openfort token for an InfraFund backend session
- keep the returned backend access token in memory, not `localStorage`
- call `backpro` directly from the browser with `credentials: 'include'`
- keep only the Openfort Shield recovery route in Next.js; do not keep the old auth proxy layer alive just to preserve Particle-era paths

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Repository preparation

- Keep active work on `openfort` in both repositories
- Update this task document to reflect the approved coordinated plan
- Create a backend-specific task document under `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/`

### Phase 2 — App-wide frontend auth integration

- Use the `useUser()` hook from `@openfort/react` as the primary auth-state source
- Implement a **client-side layout guard** (not `middleware.ts`) since Openfort session state is SDK-based and not available server-side
- Redirect authenticated users away from `/login`
- Guard app routes so unauthenticated users are redirected to `/login`
- Add loading/fallback handling while Openfort resolves session state
- Treat the existing app-shell pages as private surfaces unless intentionally split into public pages later
- Remove `AuthProvider.WALLET` from the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` (will be reintroduced in the external wallet phase)

### Phase 3 — Replace the live legacy wallet UX

- Remove or retire `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx` from the header flow
- Replace the header wallet action with Openfort-native behavior:
  - `OpenfortButton`
  - Openfort stock modal/profile flow
- Ensure the live wallet entry point is consistent with the login experience

### Phase 4 — User identity and sign-out

- Replace hardcoded guest text in `src/components/header.tsx`
- Show user identity from Openfort state
- Confirm the stock Openfort account flow covers sign-out behavior cleanly
- Confirm the post-sign-out redirect and app state reset

### Phase 5 — Frontend legacy auth cleanup ✓

**Kept (Openfort-native):**

- `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` — Shield recovery endpoint

**Deleted (legacy Particle/BFF paths):**

- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`

- `src/utils/get-server-url.ts`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`

**Replaced by:**

- `src/lib/backend-auth-client.ts` — fetch-based client for the new backend contract (`/auth/openfort/exchange`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`, `/me`)

### Phase 6 — Backend auth migration dependency

- `backpro` keeps its JWT/refresh/session architecture
- Replace Particle-specific auth inputs and validation
- Stop depending on `ParticleID` as the long-term auth identity key
- Replace it with a unique `openfort_user_id` key sourced from the validated Openfort session
- Validate the Openfort access token server-side against Openfort before issuing InfraFund JWTs
- Adopt the exchange endpoint described above as the single frontend → backend auth handshake
- Add first authenticated backend surfaces such as `/me` and account/KYC status

### Phase 7 — External wallet support (WalletConnect / MetaMask)

- Reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
- Verify WalletConnect project ID is configured and the connect flow works end-to-end
- Test MetaMask and other external wallet connections via `OpenfortWagmiBridge`
- Ensure external-wallet sessions integrate cleanly with the auth guard and header identity flow

### Phase 8 — Config hardening

- Keep Shield recovery and current Openfort provider stack
- Keep WalletConnect support wired via optional env var (`NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID`)
- Confirm target chains and sponsorship behavior for Base / Base Sepolia
- Verify environment-variable naming and required runtime fallbacks

### Phase 9 — Validation

- Run validators in both repositories after doc and code changes
- Run lint, typecheck, prettier, and targeted runtime verification in `front-pro`
- Run the relevant backend checks in `backpro`
- Manually verify:
  - login
  - redirect behavior
  - wallet creation/recovery
  - sign-out
  - header/account state
  - first backend-authenticated account flow kept in scope

16	4. sends only new users through the qualification questionnaire
17	5. defers wallet creation until after qualification
18	6. routes disqualified users to a non-resident/waitlist contact form
19	
20	## Product Direction
21	
22	- `/` becomes the public landing page with a single Openfort button.
23	- `/login` redirects to `/`.
24	- Existing users go straight from Openfort auth into the app (no onboarding).
25	- New users are qualified before the backend provisions them and a wallet is created.
26	- Disqualified users submit a non-resident contact form and stop there.
27	- No phone number, no personal-details form, no profile-verification page in this phase.
28	- If Openfort doesn't collect enough user data during auth (e.g. name via Email OTP), that gap will be addressed in a follow-up phase after manual QA, not preemptively.
29	
30	## Design Decision: Auth Before Qualification
31	
32	The old flow (landing-pro) showed the questionnaire first, then redirected to a separate dashboard app for Particle registration via a cookie handoff. With Openfort, we use a single app and a single button:
33	
34	1. User clicks the Openfort button → authenticates (Google, Email OTP, etc.).
35	2. No wallet is created (`connectOnLogin: false`, `embeddedState` stays at `EMBEDDED_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`).
36	3. Frontend calls the backend with the Openfort access token to check if the user already exists.
37	4. **Existing user** → backend session exchange → enter the app.
38	5. **New user** → qualification questionnaire → if qualified, exchange with role/type → create wallet → enter the app.
39	
40	This eliminates the two-app architecture, the cookie handoff, and the need for separate login/register buttons. Openfort handles both login and signup as one flow — the backend lookup determines which path the user takes.
41	
42	## Clean / Lean / Defaults-First Principles
43	
44	- Keep Openfort stock UI and modal behavior wherever possible.
45	- Do not restore the old Particle cookie handoff or popup chain.
46	- Keep frontend state local (`sessionStorage` for short-lived onboarding intent only).
47	- Keep backend responsibility limited to app identity, session, profile, and authorization.
48	- Do not couple onboarding to custom wallet UI.
49	- Do not add a profile-verification page preemptively. Start lean, add later if needed.
50	
51	## Backend Role
52	
53	The backend is not the wallet creator. Its job is to:
54	
55	1. verify the Openfort session/token
56	2. find the InfraFund user by `openfort_user_id`
57	3. create or refresh the InfraFund app session
58	4. expose app-level identity/status/profile endpoints
59	5. store app-specific profile data such as role, type, and completion fields
60	
61	Openfort remains responsible for authentication, embedded wallet lifecycle, and recovery.
62	
63	## Target User Flow
64	
65	```mermaid
66	flowchart TD
67	  LP[Public landing /] --> OB[Single Openfort button]
68	  OB --> OA[Openfort auth — no wallet created]
69	  OA --> CK{Backend: user exists?}
70	  CK -->|existing user| EX[Backend session exchange]
71	  EX --> APP[/home]
72	  CK -->|new user| Q1[Step 1: Role selection]
73	  Q1 --> Q2[Step 2: Individual or Organization]
74	  Q2 --> Q3[Step 3: Qualification checkboxes]
75	  Q3 -->|all confirmed| NX[Backend session exchange with role/type]
76	  NX --> WC[Create embedded wallet]
77	  WC --> APP
78	  Q3 -->|disqualified| WL[Non-resident contact form]
79	  WL --> DONE[Thank you / close]
80	```
81	
82	## Qualification Questionnaire Specification
83	
84	Ported from `landing-pro/src/component/SurveyOnlyForm.tsx`. The original had 6 steps; we keep steps 1–3 and the non-resident form (step 4). Steps 5–6 (personal details + email/ToS) are dropped because Openfort already collected email/name during auth.
85	
86	### Step 1 — "What brings you to InfraFund?" (role selection)
87	
88	| Option | Role value | Description |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| Raise Funds (Project Developer) | `client` | Project owner/developer seeking capital |
91	| Invest in Assets (Investor) | `investor` | Wants to fund green projects |
92	| Manage Construction (Contractor) | `contractor` | EPC/General Contractor |
93	| Join the DAO (Governance Member) | `governance` | Protocol governance participant |
94	
95	Note: The landing-pro code uses `dao` as the role value for governance; the backend uses `governance`. Map `dao` → `governance` at the point of exchange.
96	
97	### Step 2 — "Are you an Individual or Organization?" (type selection)
98	
99	Two cards: **Individual** or **Organization**. Maps to `type: "individual" | "organization"`.
100	
101	### Step 3 — "First, please confirm the following." (qualification checkboxes)
102	
103	**Individual (3 checkboxes, all start checked):**
104	
105	| Checkbox | Key | Disqualification message |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| I am currently a UK resident | `ukResident` | We are currently only accepting investments from UK residents. |
108	| I have a valid UK national insurance number | `niNumber` | A valid UK national insurance number is required. |
109	| I am at least 18 years old | `over18` | We do not provide services to individuals under 18 years old. |
110	
111	- If `ukResident` or `niNumber` is unchecked → disqualified → show non-resident contact form.
112	- If `over18` is unchecked → blocked (cannot continue), but not sent to contact form.
113	
114	**Organization (3 checkboxes, all start checked):**
115	
116	| Checkbox | Key | Disqualification message |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| Our company is based in UK | `ukBased` | We are currently only accepting investments from UK-based companies. |
119	| We have a valid UK Companies House number | `companyHouse` | A valid UK Companies House number is required. |
120	| Our company is currently active | `active` | We only accept applications from currently active companies. |
121	
122	- If any checkbox is unchecked → disqualified → show non-resident contact form.
123	
124	### Non-resident contact form (disqualified users)
125	
126	Shows a disclaimer: "Unfortunately, at this point in time, we cannot accept investments from [people who are not UK residents / organizations who are not in the UK]."
127	
128	Fields:
129	- First Name / Last Name (individual) or Contact Full Name / Company Name (organization)
130	- Country (dropdown from backend `/locations` endpoint)
131	- Email
132	
133	Submits to the backend non-resident endpoint (`/non-resident/individual` or `/non-resident/company`) with captcha. On success, close the modal.
134	
135	## Frontend Plan
136	
137	### 1. Deferred wallet creation config
138	
139	Set `connectOnLogin: false` in the `walletConfig` passed to `OpenfortProvider` in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`.
140	
141	```tsx
142	walletConfig={{
143	  shieldPublishableKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY,
144	  ethereum: { chainId: targetChainId },
145	  connectOnLogin: false,  // Auth without wallet creation
146	  createEncryptedSessionEndpoint: "/api/auth/encryption-session",
147	}}
148	```
149	
150	After qualification, create the wallet via:
151	```tsx
152	const { create } = useEthereumEmbeddedWallet();
153	await create({ recoveryMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC });
154	```
155	
156	### 2. Public/auth routing cleanup
157	
158	- Make `/` public — render the landing page with the Openfort button.
159	- Redirect `/login` to `/`.
160	- Replace the current implicit "everything except /login is private" rule in `main-layout.tsx` with an explicit private-route list.
161	
162	### 3. Existing-user detection after Openfort auth
163	
164	- After Openfort auth succeeds, call a backend endpoint to check whether the user exists by `openfort_user_id`.
165	- If the user exists → complete backend session exchange → enter the app.
166	- If the user is new → hold the Openfort session client-side → show qualification questionnaire.
167	- This requires either:
168	  - (a) The existing exchange endpoint to return an `is_new_user` flag, or
169	  - (b) A new lightweight lookup endpoint (e.g. `GET /v1/auth/openfort/check`) that returns `{ exists: boolean }` without creating a user.
170	
171	Option (b) is leaner — it avoids creating a user record before qualification.
172	
173	### 4. Qualification questionnaire (new component)
174	
175	- Build as a modal with steps 1–3 from the spec above.
176	- Port the UI patterns from `landing-pro/src/component/SurveyOnlyForm.tsx` but adapted to the front-pro design system (existing `Modal`, `FormInput`, `CustomButton`, `CustomCheckbox` components in `src/components/ui/`).
177	- Store qualification result in `sessionStorage` (`role`, `type`) until exchange completes.
178	- On qualification success → call backend exchange with `role` and `type` in request body → create wallet → redirect to `/home`.
179	- On disqualification → show the non-resident contact form.
180	
181	### 5. Non-resident contact form (disqualified users)
182	
183	- Reuse the backend's existing non-resident endpoints.
184	- Show the country dropdown (fetch from backend `/locations` endpoint).
185	- Submit with captcha protection.
186	- On success → show confirmation → close modal.
187	
188	### 6. Wallet creation after qualification
189	
190	- Only after the backend exchange succeeds and the user is provisioned.
191	- Use `useEthereumEmbeddedWallet().create({ recoveryMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC })`.
192	- Show a brief loading state during wallet creation ("Setting up your wallet...").
193	- Once `embeddedState` reaches `READY` (state 4) → redirect to `/home`.
194	
195	## Backend Plan
196	
197	### Current state (what exists)

200	|---|---|
201	| `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange` | Exists — validates Openfort token, creates or finds user, returns JWT |
202	| `POST /v1/auth/refresh` | Exists |
203	| `POST /v1/auth/logout` | Exists |
204	| `GET /v1/me` | Exists — returns user profile |
205	| `GET /v1/account/status` | Exists |
206	| `GET /v1/kyc/status` | Exists |
207	| `is_new_user` flag in exchange response | **Missing** — exchange detects new-vs-existing internally but doesn't expose it |
208	| `PATCH /v1/me` profile update | **Missing** — no update endpoint, no repository Update method |
209	| User repository `Update` method | **Missing** — only `Create`, `GetByOpenfortUserID`, `GetByID` |
210	| Non-resident/waitlist endpoints | **Exists in landing-pro backend** — verify availability in backpro |
211	
212	### Required backend changes
213	
214	1. **New-user detection** — Add one of:
215	   - (preferred) `GET /v1/auth/openfort/check` — authenticated endpoint that returns `{ exists: boolean }` without creating a user.
216	   - (alternative) Add `is_new_user: boolean` field to the exchange response DTO.
217	
218	2. **Non-resident endpoints** — Verify that `POST /v1/non-resident/individual` and `POST /v1/non-resident/company` (or equivalent waitlist endpoints) exist in backpro. If they only exist in landing-pro's backend proxy, they need to be added or confirmed as reachable from front-pro.
219	
220	3. **Profile update (deferred)** — Not needed in this phase. If Openfort doesn't provide sufficient user data (name via Email OTP), add `PATCH /v1/me` in a follow-up.
221	
222	## Implementation Order
223	
224	1. Set `connectOnLogin: false` in openfort-config.tsx.
225	2. Make `/` public with landing content and Openfort button; redirect `/login` to `/`.
226	3. Add backend new-user check endpoint (or `is_new_user` flag on exchange).
227	4. Update auth-session-provider to branch existing vs new users after Openfort auth.
228	5. Build the qualification questionnaire component (steps 1–3).
229	6. Build the non-resident contact form for disqualified users.
230	7. Wire wallet creation (`useEthereumEmbeddedWallet().create()`) after successful exchange.
231	8. Remove stale Particle env vars from Dockerfile and deploy workflows.
232	9. Run validators and manual QA.

# v0.2.2 Openfort Implementation With Onboarding

**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Status:** Approved plan (revised)
**Supersedes:** `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`

## Goal

Finish the Openfort rollout with a lean onboarding flow that:

1. keeps Openfort as the single auth entry point (no separate login/register buttons)
2. uses `connectOnLogin: false` so Openfort authenticates without creating a wallet
3. checks the backend to determine whether the Openfort user already exists
4. sends only new users through the qualification questionnaire
5. defers wallet creation until after qualification
6. routes disqualified users to a non-resident/waitlist contact form

## Product Direction

- `/` becomes the public landing page with a single Openfort button.
- `/login` redirects to `/`.
- Existing users go straight from Openfort auth into the app (no onboarding).
- New users are qualified before the backend provisions them and a wallet is created.
- Disqualified users submit a non-resident contact form and stop there.
- No phone number, no personal-details form, no profile-verification page in this phase.
- If Openfort doesn't collect enough user data during auth (e.g. name via Email OTP), that gap will be addressed in a follow-up phase after manual QA, not preemptively.

## Design Decision: Auth Before Qualification

The old flow (landing-pro) showed the questionnaire first, then redirected to a separate dashboard app for Particle registration via a cookie handoff. With Openfort, we use a single app and a single button:

1. User clicks the Openfort button → authenticates (Google, Email OTP, etc.).
2. No wallet is created (`connectOnLogin: false`, `embeddedState` stays at `EMBEDDED_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`).
3. Frontend calls the backend with the Openfort access token to check if the user already exists.
4. **Existing user** → backend session exchange → enter the app.
5. **New user** → qualification questionnaire → if qualified, exchange with role/type → create wallet → enter the app.

This eliminates the two-app architecture, the cookie handoff, and the need for separate login/register buttons. Openfort handles both login and signup as one flow — the backend lookup determines which path the user takes.

## Clean / Lean / Defaults-First Principles

- Keep Openfort stock UI and modal behavior wherever possible.
- Do not restore the old Particle cookie handoff or popup chain.
- Keep frontend state local (`sessionStorage` for short-lived onboarding intent only).
- Keep backend responsibility limited to app identity, session, profile, and authorization.
- Do not couple onboarding to custom wallet UI.
- Do not add a profile-verification page preemptively. Start lean, add later if needed.

## Backend Role

The backend is not the wallet creator. Its job is to:

1. verify the Openfort session/token
2. find the InfraFund user by `openfort_user_id`
3. create or refresh the InfraFund app session
4. expose app-level identity/status/profile endpoints
5. store app-specific profile data such as role, type, and completion fields

Openfort remains responsible for authentication, embedded wallet lifecycle, and recovery.

## Target User Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LP[Public landing /] --> OB[Single Openfort button]
  OB --> OA[Openfort auth — no wallet created]
  OA --> CK{Backend: user exists?}
  CK -->|existing user| EX[Backend session exchange]
  EX --> APP[/home]
  CK -->|new user| Q1[Step 1: Role selection]
  Q1 --> Q2[Step 2: Individual or Organization]
  Q2 --> Q3[Step 3: Qualification checkboxes]
  Q3 -->|all confirmed| NX[Backend session exchange with role/type]
  NX --> WC[Create embedded wallet]
  WC --> APP
  Q3 -->|disqualified| WL[Non-resident contact form]
  WL --> DONE[Thank you / close]
```

## Qualification Questionnaire Specification

Ported from `landing-pro/src/component/SurveyOnlyForm.tsx`. The original had 6 steps; we keep steps 1–3 and the non-resident form (step 4). Steps 5–6 (personal details + email/ToS) are dropped because Openfort already collected email/name during auth.

### Step 1 — "What brings you to InfraFund?" (role selection)

| Option | Role value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Raise Funds (Project Developer) | `client` | Project owner/developer seeking capital |
| Invest in Assets (Investor) | `investor` | Wants to fund green projects |
| Manage Construction (Contractor) | `contractor` | EPC/General Contractor |
| Join the DAO (Governance Member) | `governance` | Protocol governance participant |

Note: The landing-pro code uses `dao` as the role value for governance; the backend uses `governance`. Map `dao` → `governance` at the point of exchange.

### Step 2 — "Are you an Individual or Organization?" (type selection)

Two cards: **Individual** or **Organization**. Maps to `type: "individual" | "organization"`.

### Step 3 — "First, please confirm the following." (qualification checkboxes)

**Individual (3 checkboxes, all start checked):**

| Checkbox | Key | Disqualification message |
|---|---|---|
| I am currently a UK resident | `ukResident` | We are currently only accepting investments from UK residents. |
| I have a valid UK national insurance number | `niNumber` | A valid UK national insurance number is required. |
| I am at least 18 years old | `over18` | We do not provide services to individuals under 18 years old. |

- If `ukResident` or `niNumber` is unchecked → disqualified → show non-resident contact form.
- If `over18` is unchecked → blocked (cannot continue), but not sent to contact form.

**Organization (3 checkboxes, all start checked):**

| Checkbox | Key | Disqualification message |
|---|---|---|
| Our company is based in UK | `ukBased` | We are currently only accepting investments from UK-based companies. |
| We have a valid UK Companies House number | `companyHouse` | A valid UK Companies House number is required. |
| Our company is currently active | `active` | We only accept applications from currently active companies. |

- If any checkbox is unchecked → disqualified → show non-resident contact form.

### Non-resident contact form (disqualified users)

Shows a disclaimer: "Unfortunately, at this point in time, we cannot accept investments from [people who are not UK residents / organizations who are not in the UK]."

Fields:
- First Name / Last Name (individual) or Contact Full Name / Company Name (organization)
- Country (dropdown from backend `/locations` endpoint)
- Email

Submits to the backend non-resident endpoint (`/non-resident/individual` or `/non-resident/company`) with captcha. On success, close the modal.

## Frontend Plan

### 1. Deferred wallet creation config

Set `connectOnLogin: false` in the `walletConfig` passed to `OpenfortProvider` in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`.

```tsx
walletConfig={{
  shieldPublishableKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY,
  ethereum: { chainId: targetChainId },
  connectOnLogin: false,  // Auth without wallet creation
  createEncryptedSessionEndpoint: "/api/auth/encryption-session",
}}
```

After qualification, create the wallet via:
```tsx
const { create } = useEthereumEmbeddedWallet();
await create({ recoveryMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC });
```

### 2. Public/auth routing cleanup

- Make `/` public — render the landing page with the Openfort button.
- Redirect `/login` to `/`.
- Replace the current implicit "everything except /login is private" rule in `main-layout.tsx` with an explicit private-route list.

### 3. Existing-user detection after Openfort auth

- After Openfort auth succeeds, call a backend endpoint to check whether the user exists by `openfort_user_id`.
- If the user exists → complete backend session exchange → enter the app.
- If the user is new → hold the Openfort session client-side → show qualification questionnaire.
- This requires either:
  - (a) The existing exchange endpoint to return an `is_new_user` flag, or
  - (b) A new lightweight lookup endpoint (e.g. `GET /v1/auth/openfort/check`) that returns `{ exists: boolean }` without creating a user.

Option (b) is leaner — it avoids creating a user record before qualification.

### 4. Qualification questionnaire (new component)

- Build as a modal with steps 1–3 from the spec above.
- Port the UI patterns from `landing-pro/src/component/SurveyOnlyForm.tsx` but adapted to the front-pro design system (existing `Modal`, `FormInput`, `CustomButton`, `CustomCheckbox` components in `src/components/ui/`).
- Store qualification result in `sessionStorage` (`role`, `type`) until exchange completes.
- On qualification success → call backend exchange with `role` and `type` in request body → create wallet → redirect to `/home`.
- On disqualification → show the non-resident contact form.

### 5. Non-resident contact form (disqualified users)

- Reuse the backend's existing non-resident endpoints.
- Show the country dropdown (fetch from backend `/locations` endpoint).
- Submit with captcha protection.
- On success → show confirmation → close modal.

### 6. Wallet creation after qualification

- Only after the backend exchange succeeds and the user is provisioned.
- Use `useEthereumEmbeddedWallet().create({ recoveryMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC })`.
- Show a brief loading state during wallet creation ("Setting up your wallet...").
- Once `embeddedState` reaches `READY` (state 4) → redirect to `/home`.

## Backend Plan

### Current state (what exists)

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange` | Exists — validates Openfort token, creates or finds user, returns JWT |
| `POST /v1/auth/refresh` | Exists |
| `POST /v1/auth/logout` | Exists |
| `GET /v1/me` | Exists — returns user profile |
| `GET /v1/account/status` | Exists |
| `GET /v1/kyc/status` | Exists |
| `is_new_user` flag in exchange response | **Missing** — exchange detects new-vs-existing internally but doesn't expose it |
| `PATCH /v1/me` profile update | **Missing** — no update endpoint, no repository Update method |
| User repository `Update` method | **Missing** — only `Create`, `GetByOpenfortUserID`, `GetByID` |
| Non-resident/waitlist endpoints | **Exists in landing-pro backend** — verify availability in backpro |

### Required backend changes

1. **New-user detection** — Add one of:
   - (preferred) `GET /v1/auth/openfort/check` — authenticated endpoint that returns `{ exists: boolean }` without creating a user.
   - (alternative) Add `is_new_user: boolean` field to the exchange response DTO.

2. **Non-resident endpoints** — Verify that `POST /v1/non-resident/individual` and `POST /v1/non-resident/company` (or equivalent waitlist endpoints) exist in backpro. If they only exist in landing-pro's backend proxy, they need to be added or confirmed as reachable from front-pro.

3. **Profile update (deferred)** — Not needed in this phase. If Openfort doesn't provide sufficient user data (name via Email OTP), add `PATCH /v1/me` in a follow-up.

## Implementation Order

1. Set `connectOnLogin: false` in openfort-config.tsx.
2. Make `/` public with landing content and Openfort button; redirect `/login` to `/`.
3. Add backend new-user check endpoint (or `is_new_user` flag on exchange).
4. Update auth-session-provider to branch existing vs new users after Openfort auth.
5. Build the qualification questionnaire component (steps 1–3).
6. Build the non-resident contact form for disqualified users.
7. Wire wallet creation (`useEthereumEmbeddedWallet().create()`) after successful exchange.
8. Remove stale Particle env vars from Dockerfile and deploy workflows.
9. Run validators and manual QA.

## Start Here If Implementing From Blank

Use this document as the execution anchor, then open these files first:

### Frontend starting points

- `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` — add `connectOnLogin: false`
- `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx` — add new-user branching
- `src/components/main-layout.tsx` — make `/` public
- `src/app/page.tsx` — landing page with Openfort button
- `src/app/login/page.tsx` — redirect to `/`

### Reference for questionnaire

- `../landing-pro/src/component/waitlistmodal.tsx` — waitlist modal reference
- `../landing-pro/src/schema/survey.schema.ts` — validation schemas

### Backend starting points

- `../backpro/internal/application/auth/auth.go` — add check/lookup method
- `../backpro/internal/interfaces/rest/handler/auth.go` — add check endpoint handler
- `../backpro/internal/interfaces/rest/router/auth.go` — add route
- `../backpro/internal/application/auth/dto/openfort_exchange.go` — optionally add `is_new_user`
- `../backpro/internal/interfaces/rest/handler/waitlist.go` — verify non-resident endpoints

## Expected New Frontend Files

- `src/components/auth/qualification-questionnaire.tsx` — multi-step qualification modal
- `src/components/auth/non-resident-form.tsx` — contact form for disqualified users

## Expected Modified Frontend Files

- `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` — `connectOnLogin: false`
- `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx` — new-user branching + wallet creation
- `src/components/main-layout.tsx` — public route for `/`

- `deployment/Dockerfile` — remove Particle build args
- `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yaml` — update env vars
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yaml` — update env vars

## Config / Deployment

### Environment variable status

| Variable | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY` | Already in `.env.example` | Must match `INFRA_AUTH_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` in backpro |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY` | Already in `.env.example` | |
| `SHIELD_SECRET_KEY` | Already in `.env.example` | Server-side only |
| `SHIELD_ENCRYPTION_SHARE` | Already in `.env.example` | Server-side only |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Already in `.env.example` | Backend API base URL. For local: `http://localhost:8080/v1` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID` | Already in `.env.example` | Optional for this phase |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POLICY_ID` | Verify | Gas sponsorship policy — may not be set yet |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | **Needs adding** | Reuse existing key from landing-pro. Required for non-resident form captcha. |

### Dockerfile build args — remove stale Particle vars

Currently in `deployment/Dockerfile`:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID` — **remove** (Particle)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLIENT_KEY` — **remove** (Particle)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ID` — **remove** (Particle)

Replace with Openfort vars:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`

### GitHub workflow secrets — verify

Both `deploy-dev.yaml` and `deploy.yaml` trigger on push to develop/main respectively. Verify that the GitHub repo secrets include the Openfort keys and that the workflow passes them as build args to Docker.

### Backend env vars (backpro)

| Variable | Status |
|---|---|
| `INFRA_AUTH_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` | Should already be set |

| `INFRA_AUTH_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Needs setting — must match frontend `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY` |
| `INFRA_REST_COOKIE_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` | Should already be set |
| `INFRA_POSTGRES_*` (host/port/user/pass/db) | Should already be set |
| `INFRA_REST_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Verify — defaults to localhost:3000 |

### Local testing note

Use `localhost` consistently across both repos (not mixed with `127.0.0.1`). Browsers treat these as different origins for cookies and CORS.

## Validation Plan

### Frontend

- `npm run format:prettier`
- `npm run format:lint`
- `tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run build` (after auth-routing changes reach a milestone)

### Backend

- `make generate` (if SQL/repo interfaces change)
- `go build ./cmd/api`
- `go test ./...`

### Manual QA

- existing user login → straight to /home
- new qualified user → questionnaire → wallet creation → /home
- new disqualified user → non-resident form → submit → thank you
- refresh/session restore
- logout
- deferred wallet creation only happens after qualification

## Known Decisions To Preserve

- Single Openfort button on `/` (no separate login/register)
- `/login` redirects to `/`
- Existing users skip onboarding entirely
- New users go through qualification (steps 1–3)
- Disqualified users go to non-resident contact form
- Qualified users get wallet created after exchange
- No phone number collection in this phase
- No profile-verification page in this phase (add later if needed)
- Wallet creation is deferred until after qualification (`connectOnLogin: false`)
- Backend remains app-session/profile authority, not wallet authority

## Resolved Questions

1. **Captcha for non-resident form** — Reuse the existing reCAPTCHA site key from landing-pro. Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` to front-pro's env config. The reCAPTCHA v3 script is loaded via `next/script` and tokens are generated client-side with `grecaptcha.execute()`. Port the small `getRecaptchaToken()` utility from `landing-pro/src/utils/recaptcha.ts`.

2. **Non-resident endpoints** — They exist **directly in backpro**, not just as landing-pro proxies. Landing-pro's `/api/non-resident/*` routes were just Next.js proxies to backpro. Front-pro can call backpro directly:
   - `POST /v1/non-resident-waitlist/individual` (first_name, last_name, email, country_id + `X-Captcha-Token` header)
   - `POST /v1/non-resident-waitlist/company` (+ company_name)
   - `GET /v1/locations/countries` (for country dropdown, no captcha)

3. **Name collection** — Defer to a later phase. Google auth provides name + email; Email OTP provides email only. If name is missing, show it on the user's account/profile page after they enter the app and let them fill in the blanks. Do not add a pre-entry name collection step in this phase. Email/account changes should go through Openfort's own account management flow.

## Reference Material

### Frontend / repo context

- Previous task doc: `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- Review context: `docs-dev/audit-review/v0.2.0-openfort-integration-review-1.md`

- Embedded wallet notes: `docs-dev/openfort/openfort-embedded-wallet-setup.md`
- Viem/Openfort notes: `docs-dev/openfort/Developer-Guide-Viem+Openfort.md`

### Questionnaire source

- `../landing-pro/src/component/SurveyOnlyForm.tsx` — full 6-step survey
- `../landing-pro/src/component/waitlistmodal.tsx` — waitlist modal
- `../landing-pro/src/schema/survey.schema.ts` — zod validation schemas

### Backend / sibling repo context

- `../backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- `../backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.2-openfort-backend-migration-part-2.md`
- `../backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.3-openfort-backend-e2e-prep.md`

### Openfort docs / tools

- Official AI/docs entrypoint: `https://www.openfort.io/docs/overview/building-with-ai`
- Wallet configuration (connectOnLogin): `https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react/wallet`
- Wallet lifecycle states: `https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/wallet-lifecycle`
- Wallet creation API: `https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react/wallet/create`
- Access-token validation: `https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/server/access-token`
- User sessions: `https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions`
- The repo already notes Openfort AI tooling in `docs-dev/openfort/openfort-resources.md`

## Notes

- This plan intentionally replaces the earlier "implementation mostly complete" framing from `v0.2.1`.
- The older task file is retained only as historical context and should no longer be used as the execution source of truth.
- The questionnaire is ported from `landing-pro` (a separate landing page repo) where it was a 6-step flow with cookie-based handoff to the dashboard app. We keep steps 1–3 + the non-resident form, drop the personal-details and email/ToS steps since Openfort handles those during auth.

- Close the Openfort modal when finalizing authenticated sessions
- Deduplicate repeated frontend bootstrap attempts that were spamming `GET /auth/openfort/check`

### Still to verify

- Existing InfraFund user path skips onboarding and goes straight to `/home`

- Session restore/logout full pass after a successful local exchange cycle

## Required frontend env vars

| Variable | Required | Purpose | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY` | Yes | Openfort project publishable key used by the frontend auth SDK | Openfort dashboard / existing backend config |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY` | Yes | Shield publishable key used by the embedded wallet client config | Openfort Shield setup |
| `SHIELD_SECRET_KEY` | Yes | Server-side secret used by `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` | Openfort Shield setup |
| `SHIELD_ENCRYPTION_SHARE` | Yes | Server-side encryption share sent to Shield when creating an encryption session | Openfort Shield setup |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Yes | Backend API base URL. For local testing use the local backend base URL | Local backend runtime |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID` | No | Enables external wallet support | WalletConnect dashboard |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POLICY_ID` | No | Gas sponsorship policy id for transactions | Openfort dashboard |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | Needed for non-resident flow | Enables waitlist captcha submission | Existing Google reCAPTCHA config |

## SHIELD env vars

### `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY`

- The Shield publishable key.
- Safe for the frontend.
- Used in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` as `shieldPublishableKey`.

### `SHIELD_SECRET_KEY`

- The Shield secret key.
- Server-side only.
- Used in `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` as the `x-api-secret` header.

### `SHIELD_ENCRYPTION_SHARE`

- The server-side encryption share used for automatic embedded wallet recovery.
- Server-side only.
- Sent to Shield in the `/project/encryption-session` request body.

### Where to get them

Run the Openfort embedded wallet setup for the project owner account:

```bash
openfort login
openfort embedded-wallet setup
```

Then copy the values from the setup output and/or `~/.config/openfort/credentials` into `.env.local`.

If you prefer the dashboard route, get the Shield publishable/secret credentials from the Openfort project's embedded wallet / Shield configuration in the Openfort dashboard, and use the encryption share generated during embedded-wallet setup.

## Expected local backend targets

The frontend will call:

- `GET /auth/openfort/check`
- `POST /auth/openfort/exchange`
- `POST /auth/refresh`
- `POST /auth/logout`
- `GET /me`
- `GET /locations/countries`
- `POST /non-resident-waitlist/individual`
- `POST /non-resident-waitlist/company`

Because the client uses `credentials: 'include'`, backend CORS and cookies must allow the frontend origin.

## Bring-up sequence

1. Populate `.env.local` from `.env.example`.
2. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to the local backend URL.
3. Confirm backend CORS/cookie settings allow the frontend origin.
4. Start the frontend with `npm run dev`.
5. Open `/` and confirm the login screen renders.
6. Validate the Openfort login modal and embedded wallet setup flow.

## Auth flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant FE as Frontend
    participant OF as Openfort
    participant BE as Backend
    participant SH as Shield

    U->>FE: Login with Openfort
    FE->>OF: getAccessToken()
    FE->>BE: GET auth/openfort/check
    alt existing user
        FE->>BE: POST auth/openfort/exchange
        FE->>BE: GET me
        FE->>U: Redirect /home
    else new user
        FE->>U: Show qualification flow
        U->>FE: Submit onboarding
        FE->>BE: POST auth/openfort/exchange
        FE->>SH: POST encryption-session
        FE->>OF: create embedded wallet
        FE->>BE: GET me
        FE->>U: Redirect /home
    end
```

- The app does not show "Openfort is not configured."

Current status:

### 3. New user onboarding flow

- organization name validation works

- embedded wallet creation succeeds

### 4. Non-resident / disqualified flow

- submission works when reCAPTCHA is configured
- user is signed out after completion

Current status:

- Not yet exercised end-to-end
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` is still required to fully validate submission

### 5. Failure-path checks

Verify UI behavior for:

- missing Shield vars
- missing backend base URL
- backend unavailable
- CORS/cookie misconfiguration
- Shield encryption-session failure
- wallet creation failure

## Known current blockers

- Existing-user skip-onboarding flow still needs a verified known-existing user in the local backend dataset

# v0.2.2 Openfort Onboarding — Implementation Review

**Date:** 2026-04-13
**Commit reviewed:** `ae530f6` (feat(auth): add Openfort onboarding flow)
**Status:** Review complete — fixes in progress

## Validators

- `tsc --noEmit` — pass
- `eslint` — pass
- `prettier --check` — pass

## Plan Checklist

All 9 implementation items from the task plan are complete:

1. `connectOnLogin: false` in openfort-config.tsx
2. `/` public with landing + Openfort button; `/login` redirects to `/`
3. Backend new-user check endpoint call (`GET auth/openfort/check`)
4. Auth-session-provider branches existing vs new users
5. Qualification questionnaire (steps 1–3)
6. Non-resident contact form for disqualified users
7. Wallet creation after successful exchange
8. Stale Particle env vars removed from Dockerfile + workflows
9. reCAPTCHA setup (utility, Script tag, env var)

## Issues

### Fixed

#### F1. Wrong loading message during wallet creation

`src/components/main-layout.tsx` — `creating_wallet` was grouped into the generic loading state, showing "Checking your Openfort session..." while the wallet was being created. Split out `creating_wallet` to show "Setting up your wallet..." instead, matching the plan spec.

#### F2. Debug `console.log` leftover in sidebar

`src/components/sidebar.tsx:143` — `console.log(`Navigating to: ${item.url}`)` removed.

#### F3. `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` declared in Dockerfile but never passed by workflows

`deployment/Dockerfile` declared `ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` and `ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT=...` but neither `deploy-dev.yaml` nor `deploy.yaml` passes this build arg. Removed the dead ARG/ENV lines from the Dockerfile.

#### F4. Openfort modal remained open on top of InfraFund onboarding

**Files:** `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx`, `src/components/main-layout.tsx`

During local QA, a newly authenticated Openfort user could land on the InfraFund questionnaire while the Openfort wallet/create-wallet UI still remained visible underneath or above it. This broke the intended flow from the task plan, which requires Openfort auth first, then a clean branch into onboarding for new users.

**Fix:** Close the Openfort modal when:

- a new user is sent to `needs_onboarding`
- an authenticated session is finalized

Also hide the public landing content while onboarding is active so only the questionnaire is visible.

#### F5. Questionnaire modal buttons were not clickable

**File:** `src/components/ui/modal.tsx`

In local Browser MCP QA, the onboarding modal rendered but its option buttons were intermittently non-clickable, including after refresh. This was caused by stacking/pointer-event behavior around the modal layer.

**Fix:** Raise the modal wrapper z-index and make the modal panel explicitly accept pointer events.

#### F6. Repeated bootstrap calls spammed `GET /auth/openfort/check`

**File:** `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx`

Local QA showed multiple repeated `GET /v1/auth/openfort/check` requests during the same auth attempt. The app still worked, but it unnecessarily hammered the backend and cluttered logs.

**Fix:** Add a dedupe guard keyed by `openfortUserId` and `retryCount` so the bootstrap effect only runs once per auth attempt unless explicitly retried.

## Local QA status

### Verified

- Local frontend + backend bring-up completed successfully
- Email OTP login succeeded
- New-user onboarding path succeeded end-to-end
- Wallet creation occurred only after successful qualification
- Redirect to `/home` succeeded after wallet creation

### Still pending

- Existing-user skip-onboarding path with a known pre-existing backend user
- Non-resident/waitlist flow with reCAPTCHA configured
- Full refresh/logout verification pass after local exchange

### Needs Attention

#### N1. Role normalization: `client` → `project_owner`

**File:** `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx:67-68`

`normalizeRole` maps `client` → `project_owner`. The task plan lists the backend role values as `client`, `investor`, `contractor`, `governance`. It only mentions mapping `dao` → `governance`. If the backend expects `client` (not `project_owner`), new users selecting "Raise Funds" will be created with the wrong role.

**Action:** Verify with the backend what role value it expects for the "Raise Funds / Project Developer" option. If `client`, change the mapping. If `project_owner`, document the deviation from the plan.

#### N2. `wallets.length` in useCallback dependency

**File:** `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx:145`

`createWalletIfNeeded` depends on `wallets.length`. Since `wallets` comes from a hook, its `.length` is a primitive that won't update inside the memoized callback until the next render. The `wallets.length > 0` short-circuit at line 128 could evaluate against a stale value if the function is called twice (e.g. via retry after wallet creation actually succeeded).

**Risk:** Low — the current flow calls `finalizeAuthenticatedSession` right after `create()`, so this path is unlikely to be hit. Worth monitoring if duplicate wallet-creation calls appear in logs.

#### N3. Organization company name validation appears on the wrong step

**File:** `src/components/auth/qualification-questionnaire.tsx:225-228`

If a user selects "Organization" in step 2, leaves the company name empty, advances to step 3, and submits — the error "Company name is required" appears on the confirmations step (step 3), not on step 2 where the field lives. The step 2 Continue button is already disabled when `isOrganizationReady` is false, so this case requires the user to go back, fill in a name, clear it, and advance — unlikely but possible.

**Action:** Decide whether to add a guard that resets to step 2 if company name is empty when step 3 submit fires, or accept the current behavior.

#### N4. `BackendCountryRecord` dual-casing

**File:** `src/lib/backend-auth-client.ts:17-30`

The interface handles both PascalCase (`ID`, `Name`, `Iso`) and snake_case (`id`, `name`, `iso`) keys, and `normalizeCountry` resolves both. This is defensive but adds complexity. Once the backend response format is confirmed stable, simplify to whichever casing it actually returns.

#### N5. `bootstrapSession` dependency array and potential double-fire

**File:** `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx:148, 254`

`bootstrapSession` depends on `getAccessToken` from the Openfort hook. If that function's identity changes between renders, the callback recreates and the `useEffect` re-fires. The `isLoading`/`isAuthenticated` guards prevent visible double-fire, but duplicate check/exchange network calls could appear in logs.

**Action:** Monitor during QA. If duplicates appear, wrap `bootstrapSession` invocation in an `isMounted` ref guard or deduplicate with a status check.

WORKDIR /app

# Add libc6-compat for sharp/image optimization
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat

COPY package*.json package-lock.json* ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts

COPY . .

# Build args for NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY

RUN npm run build


FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init ca-certificates
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Create non-root user
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

# Copy from builder with ownership
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/package.json ./

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000

ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=40s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000', (r) => {if (r.statusCode !== 200) throw new Error(r.statusCode)})"

CMD ["dumb-init", "node", "server.js"]

name: Deploy to Dev Environment
on:
  push:
    branches: ['develop']

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build docker image
    runs-on: develop-runner
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            -f ./deployment/Dockerfile \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=${{ secrets.DEV_API_BASE_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY=${{ secrets.DEV_AUTH_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY=${{ secrets.DEV_SHIELD_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=${{ secrets.GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY }} \
            -t infra-dashboard:dev .

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Development Server
    runs-on: develop-runner
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Deploy with Docker Compose
        run: docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_DEVELOP }} up -d dashboard --force-recreate
      - name: Wait for container readiness
        run: |
          echo "Waiting for container to be ready..."
          sleep 5
          docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_DEVELOP }} ps

      - name: Verify deployment
        run: |
          docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_DEVELOP }} logs --tail=20 dashboard

name: Deploy to Production Environment
on:
  push:
    branches: ['main']

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build docker image
    runs-on: prod-runner
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            -f ./deployment/Dockerfile \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=${{ secrets.PROD_API_BASE_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY=${{ secrets.AUTH_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY=${{ secrets.SHIELD_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=${{ secrets.GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY }} \
            -t infra-dashboard:prod .

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Production Server
    runs-on: prod-runner
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Deploy with Docker Compose
        run: docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_PRODUCTION }} up -d dashboard --force-recreate
      - name: Wait for container readiness
        run: |
          echo "Waiting for container to be ready..."
          sleep 5
          docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_PRODUCTION }} ps

      - name: Verify deployment
        run: |
          docker compose -f ${{ vars.DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_PRODUCTION }} logs --tail=20 dashboard

# v0.2.4 Openfort Frontend Implementation Review

**Date:** 2026-04-15
**Reviewer:** Claude Opus 4.6
**Branch:** `openfort`
**Commits reviewed:** `35040af` → `8929654` (8 commits)
**Source-of-truth plan:** `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.2-openfort-implementation-with-onboarding.md`
**Prior review:** `docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.2-openfort-implementation-with-onboarding-review.md`

---

## Executive Summary

The 8 commits deliver the core Openfort onboarding flow specified in the v0.2.2 task plan. All 9 planned implementation items are complete. The build, TypeScript, and lint checks pass. Local QA confirmed the new-user path end-to-end (Email OTP → questionnaire → wallet creation → `/home`). Two user flows remain unverified (existing-user skip-onboarding, non-resident with reCAPTCHA). The codebase carries a few open items from the prior review, one new finding, and some deployment prep that should be tracked before merging to `develop`.

**Overall assessment:** Implementation is faithful to the plan, code quality is solid, and the remaining work is QA verification and deployment configuration — not architecture or structural gaps.

---

## Commit-by-Commit Summary

| # | Commit | Type | Summary |
|---|--------|------|---------|
| 1 | `35040af` | docs | Rewrote the v0.2.2 task plan with questionnaire spec, resolved gaps, backend status table |
| 2 | `c099de6` | chore | Removed Particle Network reference docs from the openfort branch |
| 3 | `ae530f6` | feat | **Main implementation commit** — onboarding flow, questionnaire, non-resident form, auth-session-provider rewrite, deployment cleanup (~1,584 additions) |
| 4 | `e7f5803` | fix | Wallet-creation loading message, removed debug `console.log`, removed dead `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` Dockerfile arg |
| 5 | `de939fe` | docs | Corrected embedded wallet example APIs in reference docs |
| 6 | `0b4b558` | docs | Fixed Swift/Unity examples in embedded wallet doc |
| 7 | `88a3975` | docs | Removed unused Swift/Unity/React Native sections from embedded wallet doc |
| 8 | `8929654` | fix | Isolated Openfort onboarding (modal close, deduplicate bootstrap, hide landing during onboarding), added test plan doc |

The implementation is concentrated in commits `ae530f6` and `8929654`. The remaining commits are documentation and minor cleanup.

---

## Plan Compliance

All 9 items from the v0.2.2 implementation order are addressed:

| # | Plan Item | Status | Notes |
|---|-----------|--------|-------|
| 1 | `connectOnLogin: false` in openfort-config.tsx | Done | `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx:59` |
| 2 | `/` public with landing + Openfort button; `/login` → redirect | Done | `src/app/page.tsx`, `src/app/login/page.tsx` (server-side redirect) |
| 3 | Backend new-user check (`GET auth/openfort/check`) | Done | `src/lib/backend-auth-client.ts:176-181` |
| 4 | Auth-session-provider branches existing vs new | Done | `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx:152-201` |
| 5 | Qualification questionnaire (steps 1–3) | Done | `src/components/auth/qualification-questionnaire.tsx` |
| 6 | Non-resident contact form | Done | `src/components/auth/non-resident-form.tsx` |
| 7 | Wallet creation after exchange | Done | `src/components/auth/auth-session-provider.tsx:126-150` |
| 8 | Particle env vars removed from Dockerfile + workflows | Done | Dockerfile, `deploy-dev.yaml`, `deploy.yaml` |
| 9 | reCAPTCHA setup | Done | `src/utils/recaptcha.ts`, `src/app/layout.tsx:8-16` |

### Additional plan decisions verified in code

| Decision | Verified |
|----------|----------|
| Single Openfort button on `/` (no login/register split) | Yes — `OpenfortButton` in `src/components/auth/login.tsx:26` |
| Existing users skip onboarding | Yes — `auth-session-provider.tsx:179-189` branches on `checkResponse.exists` |
| Wallet creation deferred to after qualification | Yes — `createWalletIfNeeded` called only from `completeOnboarding` |
| Disqualified users → non-resident form | Yes — `qualification-questionnaire.tsx:211-214,235` transitions to `'non_resident'` step |
| No phone number, no profile-verification page | Confirmed absent |
| Backend stays app-session authority (not wallet authority) | Yes — wallet creation is purely client-side via `useEthereumEmbeddedWallet().create()` |
| `sessionStorage` for onboarding draft (not localStorage) | Yes — keyed as `infrafund:onboarding-draft` |
| `dao` → `governance` role mapping | Yes — `auth-session-provider.tsx:71-73` |

| `tsc --noEmit` | Pass |
